title: Malaysia and the Philippines agree a framework for payments and local-currency cooperation
bank: Bank Negara Malaysia and Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas
summary: Bank Negara Malaysia and Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas signed a memorandum of understanding on 20 November. It provides a bilateral framework for cooperation in Islamic finance, cross-border payment links, local-currency transactions, financial innovation and digitalisation. The joint announcement establishes that the two governors have formalised these priorities. It gives no launch date for a service, list of participating financial institutions or change in access conditions for firms and households.

The payments and local-currency elements raise related but distinct practical questions. A payments link concerns how a transfer reaches its recipient. Local-currency use concerns the currencies in which the transaction can be made or settled. A bilateral agreement to work on both leaves room for different arrangements governing fees, exchange rates and liquidity. The announcement does not establish that a new link is operating or that traders can already settle a particular transaction in ringgit or pesos under the agreement.

Governor Abdul Rasheed Ghaffour presents the framework as a means for the institutions to learn from each other and adapt to a more complex economic and financial environment. Governor Eli Remolona emphasises the test of implementation: improvements in institutions, financial infrastructure and programmes that reach users. The signatories place the agreement in the context of regional financial integration. They give no estimate of transaction volumes, funding mobilised or costs saved. For a firm making cross-border payments, the first economically meaningful evidence will be a specified service, its eligibility rules and the price and speed available to customers.

questions.question: Which cross-border payment service will change first?
questions.detail: The two central banks name payment linkages as a field of cooperation but give no service specification. Look for a joint implementation notice identifying participating institutions, eligible users, transaction limits, fees and settlement times. A functioning service for retail transfers would have different implications from a wholesale infrastructure agreement, even if both are described as cross-border payment cooperation.

questions.question: What would make local-currency transactions commercially attractive?
questions.detail: The agreement signals interest in local currencies without specifying access to conversion or liquidity. Firms still need reliable prices at the size and times they transact. Compare subsequent settlement rules, bank quotations and any published bilateral local-currency volumes with their pre-implementation levels. Separate a shift in the settlement currency from a change in the underlying amount of bilateral trade.

questions.question: Where can users observe the effects of collaboration on Islamic finance?
questions.detail: The governors identify institutional development as a priority but attach no timetable or measured outcome. The relevant next documents would be supervisory guidance, product approvals, training milestones or market-entry decisions issued by either authority. Those releases could show whether cooperation lowers the cost of offering a product, increases access or remains an exchange of experience between the two institutions.

limitation: This is the joint signing announcement. The two authorities do not publish the text of the memorandum on this page.
